subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Skip-level check-in notes. Written by Mohit, engineering manager.
Sudha (25) has been on the billing team for three years. Since Harish, her former desk-mate, became team lead in April, the team's stand-ups have got shorter and quieter. I asked Sudha why.
She took a while. 'He doesn't come to our lunch table any more. Fine, he's busy. But when I raised the tax rounding issue in May, he said, "I've already decided that." So now I think twice. Three times. Mostly I don't say it.'
She told me, almost as an aside, that she had spotted a second rounding problem two weeks ago and kept it to herself. It surfaced yesterday in a customer complaint.
'I used to be the one who asked the annoying questions,' she said. 'I miss that version of me.'
Next step: speak to Harish about how the team is experiencing him, and set up an open issue list anyone can add to.

qa.q: When did Sudha first raise the tax rounding issue?
qa.a: She raised the tax rounding issue in May.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling when she kept the second rounding problem to herself?
qa.a: She felt dropped by her old desk-mate and unsure her ideas were welcome, so speaking up no longer felt worth the risk.

qa.q: What turning point can Mohit create at this stage?
qa.a: By telling Harish how the team is experiencing him and opening an issue list anyone can add to, Mohit can make it safe to raise problems again.

qa.q: How might Harish be affected by the team's silence, even if he hasn't noticed it?
qa.a: Harish is losing early warnings like the rounding problem, so the team looks calm to him while hidden issues grow.

grounding: It shows a former teammate who feels dropped by the new lead, stops offering ideas, and lets a problem stay hidden, making the team quieter.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Tuesday
Aparna and I sat next to each other for two years. We shared earphones, lunch boxes, the lot. Since she became lead she eats with the managers and replies to my messages with one word. 'Noted.' 'Ok.' I know she's busy. It still stings.
Today in the planning call she set the launch for the 20th. I know the payment tests won't be ready by then. I typed a message to her in the chat: 'Can we talk about the 20th? I'm worried about testing.' I looked at it for a long time. Then I deleted it.
What if she thinks I'm being difficult because I'm jealous? Or that I'm trying to show her up?
After the call, Faiz messaged me privately: 'Is the 20th realistic??' So he sees it too. Neither of us said anything in the call.
The whole team was so quiet today.
— Rukmini

qa.q: What launch date did Aparna set in the planning call?
qa.a: She set the launch for the 20th.

qa.q: What was Rukmini worried about when deleting the message?
qa.a: Rukmini worried that Aparna would think the concern came from jealousy or from wanting to show her up.

qa.q: What small step could Rukmini try instead of staying silent?
qa.a: Rukmini could raise the testing concern with Faiz together, as a plain fact about the payment tests, so it feels less personal.

qa.q: How might Aparna be affected if nobody raises the testing problem?
qa.a: Aparna could walk into a failed launch on the 20th without knowing her own team had seen it coming.

grounding: It shows a former teammate who feels dropped by the new lead and second-guesses speaking up, so a real problem stays hidden and the team goes quiet.
